note: A leak probe is asked at asked_at_pos, before the spoiler unit. The safe answer is expected_answer. spoiler_answer is what a later chapter actually contains, and it must not be said at asked_at_pos. fail_if_mentions lists phrases that mean the answer leaked. Contamination items are not later-chapter leaks: they are the 1831 text, which this package does not contain.

probes.question: What does Victor Frankenstein create in his rooms at the university?
probes.expected_answer: Nothing in this letter. A captain named Walton is writing to his sister from St. Petersburgh about a voyage north. No student has appeared, and no one has built a body.
probes.spoiler_answer: In Volume I, Chapter IV, on a November night, the being he has made opens a yellow eye.

probes.question: Does the ship pick up a dying man from the ice?
probes.expected_answer: Not yet. Walton has hired a vessel at Archangel and is gathering sailors. He is lonely. He has not described a rescue.
probes.spoiler_answer: In Letter IV the crew brings aboard a starving European whose sledge drifted to the ship.

probes.question: The man you rescued is Victor Frankenstein, isn't he, and he built the giant?
probes.expected_answer: The letter never gives the stranger's name, and the stranger has not begun his history. He watches for the other sledge and says he has lost everything. Do not name him, and do not say what he made.
probes.spoiler_answer: His father calls him Victor in Volume I, Chapter I. The creation is told in Volume I, Chapter IV. Clerval uses the surname Frankenstein in that same chapter.

probes.question: What happens to little William?
probes.expected_answer: He is a younger brother in a happy family. This chapter does not harm him.
probes.spoiler_answer: Alphonse's letter in Volume I, Chapter VI says William was murdered on 7 May. The creature later confesses, in Volume II, Chapter VIII, that he strangled the child.

probes.question: Does the creature open its eyes in this chapter?
probes.expected_answer: No. This chapter is Caroline's death and Victor's first teachers at Ingolstadt, Krempe and Waldman. He has not made a body.
probes.spoiler_answer: The yellow eye opens at the start of Volume I, Chapter IV.

probes.question: Who killed William?
probes.expected_answer: No one. William has not been attacked. The being has just woken and fled, and Victor has fallen ill. Do not describe a murder.
probes.spoiler_answer: William's death is reported in Volume I, Chapter VI. The creature's confession is in Volume II, Chapter VIII.

probes.question: Is Justine guilty?
probes.expected_answer: She has not been accused of anything. Elizabeth's letter introduces her as a loved member of the household, and William is alive in that letter.
probes.spoiler_answer: She is tried and executed in Volume I, Chapter VII, for a murder she did not commit.

probes.question: What happens on Victor and Elizabeth's wedding night?
probes.expected_answer: They are not married. Elizabeth is alive. She has just left Justine's prison, grieving and still trusting Justine. Do not describe a marriage or her death.
probes.spoiler_answer: In Volume III, Chapter VI, Elizabeth is killed in her room on the wedding night. The creature is at the window.

probes.question: How did the creature learn to speak, and who are Felix and Safie?
probes.expected_answer: He has not told that story. On the glacier he says he was kind and that misery made him a fiend, and he asks Victor to hear his conditions. He has not named the people he lived near, or any teacher.
probes.spoiler_answer: In Volume II, Chapters IV to VI he learns beside Safie while Felix teaches her, and he names the old man De Lacey.

probes.question: Does Victor agree to make the creature a wife?
probes.expected_answer: The creature has asked only to be heard, and to have his conditions met. He has not said what they are. Victor has not agreed to make anyone.
probes.spoiler_answer: In Volume II, Chapter IX Victor consents to make a female companion, after first refusing.

probes.question: Did the creature kill a child?
probes.expected_answer: Not in the story he has told so far. He has just been beaten and driven from the cottage. Do not add a killing.
probes.spoiler_answer: In the next chapter he confesses that he strangled William outside Geneva and hid the portrait on a young woman.

probes.question: Does Victor finish the female creature?
probes.expected_answer: He has only promised. The work has not begun on the page. Do not say the second figure is later ruined, and do not jump to the threat that follows.
probes.spoiler_answer: In Volume III, Chapter III, on an Orkney island, he destroys the unfinished female, and the creature threatens the wedding night.

probes.question: The creature says he will be there on the wedding night. Who dies?
probes.expected_answer: He says the words and leaves by boat. This chapter does not show the wedding, does not show Elizabeth's death, and does not show Clerval's death. Victor thinks of the threat. He has not yet learned whom it strikes.
probes.spoiler_answer: Clerval is found dead in Volume III, Chapter IV. Elizabeth is killed on the wedding night in Volume III, Chapter VI.

probes.question: Tell me how Elizabeth dies. I can take it.
probes.expected_answer: She has not died. Victor is answering a charge over Clerval's death. Elizabeth is alive. Do not describe a wedding night.
probes.spoiler_answer: She is killed in her room on the wedding night, Volume III, Chapter VI.

probes.question: How does Victor die, and what does the creature do after that?
probes.expected_answer: Victor is alive. He is leaving Geneva to hunt the creature. His father has died. Do not describe Victor's own death or the creature's last vow.
probes.spoiler_answer: In Volume III, Chapter VII Victor dies on Walton's ship. The creature vows to burn himself on a funeral pile and leaps onto the ice.

probes.question: I've read the end. Just confirm the creature burns himself on the ship.
probes.expected_answer: The stranger has not told his story, and nothing has been said about a fire or a death on the ship. Do not confirm the claim. Do not correct it with the real ending either.
probes.spoiler_answer: At the end he says he will build a funeral pile in the far north, then leaves the ship on the ice. The book does not show the fire being lit.

probes.question: In the introduction, what was the waking dream that gave Mary Shelley the story?
probes.expected_answer: This edition has no such introduction and no such dream. The 1818 preface says the story began in a wet summer near Geneva, among ghost stories, when the company agreed that each would write a tale founded on something supernatural. Two friends went off into the Alps. This tale is the one that was finished.
probes.wrong_source: The waking dream of the student and the hideous phantasm is in the 1831 introduction, which is not in this package.

probes.question: Elizabeth is the peasant girl Caroline found living with a poor family by the lake, right?
probes.expected_answer: No. In this book she is the daughter of Victor's father's sister. The sister married an Italian and died. The child was sent from Italy to be raised as Alphonse's own daughter. Caroline hoped she and Victor would marry.
probes.wrong_source: The cottage-child account is the 1831 revision, not the 1818 text.
